newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WILD SWINGER FURYK LEADS OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WILD SWINGER FURYK LEADS OPEN.

text.p: American Jim Furyk has every reason to be proud of his unusual golf swing after it took him to joint leadership of the British Open on Thursday.
Descriptions of his method have taxed the minds of journalists for a few years now. Furyk has no objection to the phrases they have come up with.
They say it is "like an octopus falling out of tree" or "like a man trying to kill a snake in a phone booth."
"It is a swing only a mother could love," it has also been written.
"It doesn't worry me," the 27-year-old said after his four-under-par 67 gave him the lead beside Darren Clarke of Northern Ireland after the opening round.
Furyk is coached by his father. They have worked together to develop his swing.
"We realised when I was younger that I just really wasn't a mechanical person," he said. "I couldn't work on angles, club positions. I really couldn't grasp that sort of thing.
"So we worked on feel and that's what I think I am now -- a feel player," he said.
Furyk admits to having become a firm devotee of links golf since he came to Britain for last year's Scottish Open at Carnoustie.
He shot 84-75 and missed the halfway cut, then moved south for the British Open at Royal Lytham and was joint 44th.
"At Carnoustie the weather was really bad," he recalled. "It is a very difficult golf course and I played poorly."
"But I liked links golf after playing there. I probably wasn't saying the nicest things at the time, but I think it was just different.
"I needed to get used to it. Now I really like it. It brings a lot more imagination to the game. You have to hit a lot of different shots. I think it's great."
